rows.text: The deck is deliberately split in half. One half is cheap NON-HUMAN bodies whose only job is to attack; the other half is expensive HUMANS you never intend to cast. Winota converts the first into the second — every non-Human that attacks digs six cards deep and puts a Human onto the battlefield already attacking and indestructible. Count your non-Human attackers before combat, because that number is how many free Humans you get.

rows.name: Winota, Joiner of Forces
rows.text: every non-Human creature that attacks looks six deep and cheats a Human into play tapped, attacking and indestructible. Four mana, and a board of four tokens is four free Humans.

rows.name: Reconnaissance
rows.text: the best card in the deck. Attack with everything, let Winota trigger on each non-Human, THEN remove the fragile attackers from combat and untap them. You keep the triggers, lose nothing to blockers, and still have blockers up.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free with your commander out, and it redirects the removal spell aimed at Winota mid-combat.

rows.name: Giver of Runes
rows.text: protection from a colour every turn, for one mana, on the creature that matters.

rows.name: Flare of Fortitude
rows.text: free if you sacrifice a white creature. Your life cannot change and everything you control gains hexproof and indestructible — it beats a wrath, a burn spell and a targeted removal spell at once.
These are not filler. Each one is a Winota trigger every combat.

rows.name: Goblin Rabblemaster
rows.text: a hasty Goblin at the beginning of combat, every turn, and it forces them to attack.

rows.name: Legion Warboss
rows.text: the same effect, and mentor grows whatever it attacks alongside.

rows.name: Loyal Apprentice
rows.text: a hasty flying Thopter each combat while you control your commander.

rows.name: Ainok Strike Leader
rows.text: a Goblin per opponent whenever it or Winota attacks — three extra triggers in a four-player pod.

rows.name: Anim Pakal, Thousandth Moon
rows.text: Gnomes equal to her counter total, every attack, snowballing.

rows.name: Myrel, Shield of Argive
rows.text: Soldier tokens equal to your Soldier count on every attack, and opponents cannot interact during your turn at all.

rows.name: Okoye, Dora Milaje Leader
rows.text: two Soldiers on arrival, and your attacking tokens get first strike.

rows.name: Phoenix Chick
rows.text: one mana, flies, has haste, and it climbs back out of the graveyard whenever you attack with three creatures.

rows.name: Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer
rows.text: a Monkey, so it triggers Winota, and it steals a card and a Treasure on the way through.

rows.name: Ornithopter
rows.text: zero mana, flies, and it is a Winota trigger from turn one.

rows.name: Phyrexian Walker
rows.text: the same, on the ground.

rows.name: Ornithopter of Paradise
rows.text: a trigger that also fixes your mana.

rows.name: Hope of Ghirapur
rows.text: a flying trigger that shuts off an opponent's noncreature spells for a turn.

rows.name: Quicksilver, Brash Blur
rows.text: can start the game on the battlefield, has haste, and is not a Human.

guide.title: The Humans you want to hit

rows.name: Blade Historian
rows.text: attacking creatures have DOUBLE STRIKE. Cheated in mid-combat, it doubles the damage of the attack that put it there.

rows.name: Angrath's Marauders
rows.text: all your damage is doubled. Alongside Blade Historian your tokens hit for four times their printed power.

rows.name: Combat Celebrant
rows.text: exert it and you untap everything and get an ADDITIONAL COMBAT PHASE — which is a whole second round of Winota triggers.

rows.name: Lena, Selfless Champion
rows.text: a Soldier for every nontoken creature you control, and she sacrifices to make the team indestructible.

rows.name: Myrel, Shield of Argive
rows.text: doubles your Soldier count and locks opponents out of your turn.

rows.name: Anim Pakal, Thousandth Moon
rows.text: better cheated in than cast, because she starts making Gnomes immediately.

rows.name: Lightning, Army of One
rows.text: once she connects, every source you control deals DOUBLE damage to that player until your next turn.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: nobody can respond to anything for the rest of your turn.

rows.name: Boromir, Warden of the Tower
rows.text: counters anything cast for free, and sacrifices to make the board indestructible.

rows.name: Professional Face-Breaker
rows.text: a Treasure per combat damage step, convertible into impulse draws.

rows.name: Black Widow, Agile Avenger
rows.text: menace, and she grows and draws off the table's extra draws.

rows.name: Imperial Recruiter
rows.text: any creature with power 2 or less — which is most of your non-Human triggers.

rows.name: Recruiter of the Guard
rows.text: any creature with toughness 2 or less.

rows.name: Ranger-Captain of Eos
rows.text: finds a one-drop, and sacrifices to stop every noncreature spell for a turn. That is how you protect the alpha strike.

guide.title: Taxing them while you set up

rows.name: Archon of Emeria
rows.text: one spell per turn each, and their nonbasics enter tapped. A token deck barely notices; a combo deck dies to it.

rows.name: High Noon
rows.text: the same lockout on an enchantment, and it converts into five damage later.

rows.name: Deafening Silence
rows.text: one noncreature spell per turn each, and it never touches your creature deployment.

rows.name: Drannith Magistrate
rows.text: no casting from graveyards, exile or the command zone. It turns off every other commander at the table.

rows.name: Aven Mindcensor
rows.text: flash him onto a fetchland or a tutor.

rows.name: Aven Interrupter
rows.text: flash, exiles a spell outright, and taxes what they try to recast.

rows.name: Charismatic Conqueror
rows.text: everything they play either arrives tapped or gives you a lifelinking Vampire.

rows.name: Hexing Squelcher
rows.text: your spells cannot be countered and your creatures get ward.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell every turn.

rows.name: Ocelot Pride
rows.text: a Cat every end step you gained life, doubled once you have the city's blessing — and Cats are not Human.

rows.name: Path to Exile
rows.text: one mana, exile.

rows.name: Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd
rows.text: flash, and every attack exiles a blocker or a problem permanent for the turn.

rows.name: Flare of Fortitude
rows.text: the free save.

rows.name: Reconnaissance
rows.text: also a defensive card — remove your attackers from combat and they are untapped blockers on the crack-back.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep cheap non-Humans. Ornithopter, Phyrexian Walker and Phoenix Chick look like nothing and are the entire engine — a turn-four Winota with three non-Humans already attacking is three free Humans on turn four.

Do not cast the Humans. Blade Historian, Angrath's Marauders and Lena are all far better cheated in mid-combat, and casting them wastes both the mana and the surprise. If you must hard-cast something, cast a trigger body instead.
Attack with everything, then use Reconnaissance. The Winota triggers happen on declaration, so pulling a 1/1 out of combat afterwards costs you nothing and saves the body for next turn.

rows.name: Combat Celebrant
rows.text: the highest-value hit in the deck. An extra combat is another full round of Winota triggers, and the Humans you already cheated in are untapped for it.
